text:
noah.cust: hey, our production service started getting 403s ~10m after the deploy. response body says \"invalid_api_key\" but we didn't rotate keys. sample curl:

curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"error\": \"invalid_api_key\"
}

noah.cust: this is blocking customers, they can't complete calls. any quick checks I should run? :cry:

ellie.support: sorry about that — can you paste the request id / header dump if available? 403 looks auth-y but could be a plan/entitlement block. we had a couple of billing sync flaps last week.

noah.cust: here's verbose output (redacted):
* Connected to api.redwood.ai
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***
> Host: api.redwood.ai
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
< x-plan-status: BLOCKED
< x-plan-reason: tier_mismatch
< content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "invalid_api_key"
}

ellie.support: ah ok that header `x-plan-status: BLOCKED` is the giveaway. support -> billing -> eng: looks like entitlement service returned a plan-block but our gateway is mapping it to the generic invalid key body.

raj.eng: filing quick note: entitlement middleware currently maps non-OK entitlement states -> 403 + {error: invalid_api_key} for backward compatibility. this makes plan gating indistinguishable from real key issues. reproducible locally with tenant that has a pending invoice.

raj.eng: quick repro steps I used:
1) create test tenant w/ sku `starter-v2` via sandbox billing svc
2) mark invoice status = pending
3) call endpoint using valid API key -> gateway returns 403 + error invalid_api_key but header shows `x-plan-status: BLOCKED` and `x-plan-reason: unpaid_invoice`

paula.account: customer actually did change slots yesterday and the billing migration job was still running when the new keys were issued; sounds like a race where key issuance happened before tenant sync. we see the console as \"active\" but billing backend hasn't attached the new SKU yet.

ellie.support: for now you can ask the customer to wait ~2-3m and retry, or we can manually trigger a tenant sync for them. @paula.account can you trigger sync for tenant `acme-continental`? (request-id: req_0a1b2c3d)

paula.account: triggering now: POST /internal/tenant-sync?tenant=acme-continental

deploy-bot: tenant-sync job enqueued (job_id: job_987654). status: started.

raj.eng: proposed short-term fix (quick patch): gateway should include a distinct body or header when entitlement blocks the request. e.g.

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Entitlement: blocked
{
  "error": "plan_block",
  "reason": "unpaid_invoice"
}

raj.eng: longer term: we should avoid returning `invalid_api_key` for entitlement cases. that breaks client UX and confuses customers + support. I'll open a PR to change mapping and add telemetry to count how often this header appears.

ellie.support: thanks @raj.eng and @paula.account. escalation notes: affected customers: acme-continental (+2). impact: all token-based calls 403; workaround: tenant-sync or short wait for billing job to finish. next steps: raj -> PR for gateway mapping, paula -> confirm tenant sync completed and notify customer, ellie -> update support ticket with repro + workaround.

noah.cust: confirmed calls started working ~90s after sync completed. thanks team! :tada:

ellie.support: closing loop: we should also update docs/SDK to surface this case so integrators don't chase key rotation unnecessarily. adding a follow-up item to support backlog.
